question:
A carpenter needs to design a wooden box in the shape of a cuboid such that the sum of its length and breadth is 3 cm more than its height. Twice of its length, thrice of its breadth and its height add up to 10 cm. Its breadth added to 7 times its height is 1 cm less than 3 times its length.

On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions :

**(i)** Write the equations representing the various dimensions and express them as the matrix equation $AX=B$
**(ii)** Find if $A^{-1}$ exists. Justify your answer.
**(iii) (a)** Find $A^{-1}$.
OR
**(iii) (b)** Find $A^{2}+7~I$
explanation:
(i)

Step 1 Assign variables $x, y, z$ to represent the length, breadth, and height of the box respectively. Translating the verbal parameters into linear algebraic relationships yields: $x + y = z + 3 \implies x + y - z = 3$; then $2x + 3y + z = 10$; and finally $y + 7z = 3x - 1 \implies -3x + y + 7z = -1$.

Step 2 Arrange these equations into standard matrix equation form $AX = B$: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 7 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 10 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$.

(ii)

Step 1 To justify if $A^{-1}$ exists, evaluate the determinant of the coefficient matrix $A$ along its first row: $|A| = 1(3(7) - 1(1)) - 1(2(7) - 1(-3)) + (-1)(2(1) - 3(-3))$.

Step 2 Calculate the numeric values: $|A| = 1(20) - 1(17) - 1(11) = 20 - 17 - 11 = -8$. Since $|A| = -8 \neq 0$, matrix $A$ is non-singular, which guarantees that $A^{-1}$ exists.

(iii) (a)

Step 1 Determine the cofactor matrix components $C_{ij}$ for matrix $A$: $C_{11}=20, C_{12}=-17, C_{13}=11; C_{21}=-8, C_{22}=4, C_{23}=-4; C_{31}=4, C_{32}=-3, C_{33}=1$. Transposing this matrix yields the adjoint matrix: $\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 20 & -8 & 4 \\ -17 & 4 & -3 \\ 11 & -4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

Step 2 Apply the matrix inversion formula $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\text{adj}(A)$ to get: $A^{-1} = -\frac{1}{8}\begin{bmatrix} 20 & -8 & 4 \\ -17 & 4 & -3 \\ 11 & -4 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2.5 & 1 & -0.5 \\ 2.125 & -0.5 & 0.375 \\ -1.375 & 0.5 & -0.125 \end{bmatrix}$.

(iii) (b)

Step 1 Compute $A^2$ via matrix multiplication: $A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 7 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 7 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 3 & -7 \\ 5 & 12 & 8 \\ -22 & 7 & 53 \end{bmatrix}$.

Step 2 Combine this with the scaled identity matrix $7I$: $A^2 + 7I = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 3 & -7 \\ 5 & 12 & 8 \\ -22 & 7 & 53 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 13 & 3 & -7 \\ 5 & 19 & 8 \\ -22 & 7 & 60 \end{bmatrix}$.
